triiodothyronine replacement in hypothyroid rats, or in cultured Sertoli cell, inhibits both the proliferation of immature Sertioli cell and aromatase expression.
T(3) inhibits Sertoli cell proliferation, and this effect may be mediated, in part, by the inhibition of aromatase expression.

the identification of a new mechanism for the regulation of the expression of the aromatization enzyme in Sertoli cells.
the identification of the molecular events involved in the control of aromatase expression in prepuberal rat Sertoli cell.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of P450 arom expression in rat Sertoli cell.

T(3) down-regulates the aromatase activity of prepuberal rat Sertoli cell cultures by acting at both the mRNA and protein levels.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T(3) exerts its effects on aromatase through the modulation of both transcription and posttranscriptional events.

the thyroid hormone T(3) is a key player in the regulation of Sertoli cell proliferation, aromatase activity, and estrogen production.
